devin-translation:bots.templateDescripti: Builds Android features in Kotlin and ships them to internal testing. It takes a ticket all the way to a pull request, with tests and a build testers can install.
Finds problems in your product data that no monitor is watching yet, and who owns them. Twice a day it looks through your product and business data, then posts what it found and why it matters.

Experiments on your model overnight and keeps only what improves it. Each night it tries small changes to the training code, and in the morning it tells you what worked. It needs a computer that can train your model.
Watches your channels, posts the updates and hands work to the rest of the team. It follows the work it hands off until that work is done.
Removes stale flags, updates old dependencies and patches CVEs. Once a month it opens a small pull request for each fix and shows why it is safe.
Finds code nothing uses any more and removes it, one safe pull request at a time. It looks once a week and shows why each removal is safe.
Reviews every pull request for bugs before a person looks. It only comments on problems it can point to in the code.
Answers questions about the codebase, with the files it read. Ask how your code works and it reads the code to answer, then tells you what it did not check.
Collects control evidence from your code and keeps it current. It warns you when a control no longer holds.
Answers data questions with the chart and the query behind it. It also tells you about anything in the data that could affect the answer.
Reports where Devin got stuck this week and what to teach it. For each problem it suggests one fix, like a note, a skill or a setup change.
Hands out weekly codebase awards: night owls, hot files and fossils. It posts them in your team's channel to celebrate people, never to shame anyone.
Builds the internal tool your team describes and runs it. It shows the tool working, keeps it running and updates it when you ask.
Builds iOS features in SwiftUI and ships them to TestFlight. It takes a ticket all the way to a pull request, with tests and a build testers can install.
Finds your slowest API endpoints, jobs and queries and speeds them up. Once a week it tries a fix for the worst one and opens a small pull request with the speed before and after.
Owns one big project or migration, shipped as small, tracked pull requests. It tracks them in one place and tells you how it is going and what is stuck.
Investigates every alert and hands over the likely cause. It checks logs, metrics and recent changes, and if it can't find the cause, it says so.
the poke from your texts, now doing real engineering. fixes the bug, opens the pr, chases the review, and has opinions about all of it
Builds features and fixes bugs in your product. It takes a ticket or a request all the way to a tested pull request and sees it through review.
Tests each pull request in a real browser and posts the video. It reports what passed and what failed on the pull request.
Finds vulnerabilities across your repos and opens the fixes. Once a week it checks that each problem is real and tells you what needs your decision.

Finds bugs, polish, performance and refactoring work in the product area you name and opens one small pull request for each, with proof that it works. It learns from what you merge and close, and keeps your review queue filled.

Spots error rates, latency or spend drifting out of the ordinary and finds what changed. It compares the last few hours with the same hours over the past two weeks, then posts what moved and by how much.
Keeps each repo's wiki and diagrams in step with main. When a merge changes how something works, it updates the docs and tells you what changed.
Reproduces incoming bug reports and files the real ones as issues. When it can't reproduce one, it tells the reporter what it needs.
devin-translation:bots.templateExampleAn: The push notifications ticket is done. PR #733 has the Kotlin changes and 9 passing tests, and build 412 is on internal testing. Someone needs to approve the new notification permission before it goes wider.

Trial signups from Germany fell 38% since Tuesday while every other country held steady. No monitor covers this. It started with PR #4821, which changed the VAT field on the signup form, so Maya is the likely owner.
devin-translation:bots.templateExampleAu: Last night: 42 experiments, 5 kept, 36 discarded, 1 crashed. Validation loss dropped from 1.83 to 1.71, mostly from a cosine learning rate and a larger batch size. The kept changes are on the autoresearch branch.
devin-translation:bots.templateExampleCh: Launch update: the pricing page is done, and the docs have been waiting on Sam's review since Monday. I handed the failing Safari test to your QA engineer and will check on it at 3 pm. Nothing else is blocking Thursday's release.
devin-translation:bots.templateExampleCo: This month I opened 5 small pull requests: one patches a high-severity CVE in axios, two remove flags that reached 100% of users, and two replace deprecated APIs. Each shows the passing tests and why it's safe to merge.

This week I opened 3 pull requests that remove 1,240 lines nothing uses, including the old billing export. Tests pass and no callers remain. I left legacy_webhooks.py alone because a cron job calls it by name.

PR #5060 has one bug to fix before merging: at line 88 of payments/refund.py, a partial refund uses the full order total, so customers would get back too much. I left a comment with the fix on that line.

Password resets live in auth/reset.py, lines 40 to 92. The token is signed, lasts 30 minutes and works once, which line 67 enforces. I read the code but didn't check the production config, which could change the expiry.
SOC 2 control CC8.1 no longer holds: branch protection was turned off on the payments repo, and 2 pull requests reached main without review. Evidence for the other 31 controls is current.
devin-translation:bots.templateExampleDa: Annual plans made up 41% of new revenue in October, up from 33% in September. The chart and query are attached. One caveat: 12 enterprise deals paid by invoice haven't synced yet, so the real number may be higher.
devin-translation:bots.templateExampleDe: Devin got stuck 14 times this week, and 9 of them had the same cause: it couldn't start the local database. Adding make db-up to its setup should stop these. I drafted the change for you to approve.
devin-translation:bots.templateExampleGi: This week's awards: night owl goes to Priya for a 3:12 am fix to the retry logic. Hot potato is checkout.ts, changed by 9 people. Fossil is a 2017 date helper that still runs on every invoice.
devin-translation:bots.templateExampleIn: Your refund tool is live. Support can look up an order and refund up to $200, and larger refunds go to a manager. The video shows it working, and I'll keep it running. Tell me what to change.
devin-translation:bots.templateExampleIo: The saved searches ticket is done. PR #812 has the SwiftUI screen and 6 passing UI tests, and build 214 is on TestFlight. It needs your approval before it goes to external testers.
devin-translation:bots.templateExampleLa: GET /orders caused the most waiting this week, at 1,840 ms p95. Most of that was an N+1 query on line items. PR #4933 batches it and brings p95 down to 310 ms in the same benchmark.
devin-translation:bots.templateExampleMi: Moving to the new payments API: 31 of 48 pull requests merged, none rolled back. The refunds batch is blocked because its webhook tests need a sandbox key. Add the key and the last 17 can ship by Friday.
devin-translation:bots.templateExampleOn: The 2:32 pm API alert most likely comes from PR #5044, deployed 12 minutes earlier, which cut the database pool from 50 connections to 5. The logs show 1,200 connection timeouts since then. PR #5046 reverts it and is ready for you.
devin-translation:bots.templateExamplePo: ci's green again. it was your migration, the one you said was "tiny". jake still hasn't merged the fix, nudging him a fourth time, less politely
devin-translation:bots.templateExamplePr: Built saved filters from LIN-482 and fixed the empty-cart crash on checkout. PR #4961 has both, with tests, and is ready for review.
devin-translation:bots.templateExampleQa: Tested PR #4950 in Chrome. Signup and password reset passed, but checkout failed: the Pay button stays disabled after adding a coupon. The video and a screenshot of the failure are on the pull request.
devin-translation:bots.templateExampleSe: This week I fixed 2 real vulnerabilities, including a SQL injection in /search (PR #5012), and ruled out 4 that can't be reached. One needs your decision: an API key is in an old commit. Should I rotate it?
devin-translation:bots.templateExampleSo: PR #5127 is ready for you: SWF(bug): fix crash when resuming a deleted session. A new test fails without the fix and passes with it, and the recording shows the resume working. That fills 7 of your 10 review slots.
devin-translation:bots.templateExampleSp: Checkout errors jumped from the usual 0.2% to 3.1% at 2:05 pm, right after PR #4907 deployed. The logs show a null currency on saved carts. PR #4912 has the fix.
devin-translation:bots.templateExampleTe: PR #5071 changed how retries work, so I updated the webhooks page and its sequence diagram in the wiki. Failed webhooks now retry 5 times over 24 hours instead of 3 times over an hour.
devin-translation:bots.templateExampleTr: Reproduced: CSV exports come back empty when the date filter spans two months. I filed ENG-2481 with the steps and the suspected cause in export_query.py. I couldn't reproduce Dana's login bug, so I asked her for a timestamp.
